setting.note: A young officer abandons a crowded pilgrim ship in a moment of panic and spends the rest of the novel trying to redeem himself, finally as the trusted white man of a remote Malay river-settlement; that settlement, Patusan, is fictional, drawn from the Berau river in Borneo Conrad had known as a sailor.

rights.originalWork: First published in 1900 by Joseph Conrad; long out of copyright. Mapped as a cited work: no text stored, no passages reproduced. The places are facts and the notes are our own.
rights.textSource: None stored. A cited book reproduces no text.
rights.territoryNotes: Locations and original commentary only. No reproduction of any text, in any territory.
rights.attribution: Lord Jim, Joseph Conrad (1900). Locations mapped by Read the Places; Patusan is fictional, modelled on the Berau river in Borneo.

palette.note: The tropical river and sea Jim's whole story moves along. A cited book's colour is not a quotation; it still has to be legible, and this clears WCAG AA on paper.
